The repo's build gathers the sidecars into template-catalog.json beside template-manifest.json. Templates shipped before 0.3.1 keep theirs (they lag this rule; a sidecar overrides them).

lagging.fix: every prop that CAN carry a canvas handle is either bound on the rect that shows it (bindProp / bindProps / bindPropPath / bindPropRect) or named in template.bindings.unbound with the reason it has none ({ fps: "timing" }). A declaration naming an unknown prop, or one that is actually bound, is itself a violation — a stale entry is worse than none. Templates hashed in frozen.manifest.json are exempt.

violations.detail: source 0 is a static #e8eee9 fill covering the whole 1080×1080 canvas and no prop is bound to it — set document.backgroundColor instead and drop the source, or make the rect a handle (bindProp(src, "<the prop it should edit>") — a card bound to the theme preset is where the theme gets changed). A base rect nothing binds is a click target over everything: in Make it is selected whenever the pointer is not on a smaller tile, and the click does nothing. (A template whose SUBJECT is that rect declares it: canvas.baseRect = "<why>". A template that must ship it because it is composed INTO another uses defaultProps.useNestedBackgroundColor = true instead.)

lagging.fix: fill the canvas with document.backgroundColor, never a full-canvas colour rect that nothing binds. A base rect is a click target that covers everything — it gets selected in Make any time the pointer is not on a smaller tile — and if no prop is bound to it that click does nothing; the document background does the same job with no rect at all. Only a STATIC, fully opaque fill counts: a curtain wipe (overlay.enable / window), a scrim (overlay.alpha) and a masked shape are legitimate and never flagged — a ROUNDED or stroked card is NOT exempt from 0.3.1 on (its corners do not change what a click on it does — a repo held to 0.3.0 keeps the exemption it shipped under), but a full-canvas rect that CARRIES A HANDLE is (a card bound to the theme preset is where the theme gets changed). Two declared exceptions, and they mean different things: canvas.baseRect = "<why>" is the general one (the rect IS the subject — a lesson about full-rect nodes, a tutorial surface), and defaultProps.useNestedBackgroundColor = true is the narrow one (this template is COMPOSED INTO another, whose slot its own backgroundColor cannot fill). An empty baseRect reason is refused.

lagging.fix: every prop that CAN carry a canvas handle is either bound on the rect that shows it (bindProp / bindProps / bindPropPath / bindPropRect) or named in template.bindings.unbound with the reason it has none ({ fps: "timing" }). The accountable props are free-text and colour strings, numbers, media, one element of a basic list, one leaf of json / list / array, and a regions-picker rect; booleans, closed sets, group containers, the m0 family, code and hidden / human props are never canvas things. A declaration naming an unknown prop, or one that is actually bound, is itself a violation — a stale entry is worse than none. Templates hashed in frozen.manifest.json are exempt.
